name: An Attainable Boundary Order Lost under Contraction
definition: Let $C\subseteq Q_{12}$ be the 289-concept dismantlable ample class whose unique initial corner is $0$, translated so that it contains the bit-$1$ and bit-$2$ neighbors $2$ and $4$. Mark the boundary edge $D=\{0,2\}$ and, for a fresh coordinate $f$, form the peripheral expansion $A=(D\times\{0\})\cup(C\times\{1\})$.
properties: The corner order beginning $(2,0),(0,0)$ and continuing through the upper copy realizes boundary order $(2,0)$ with outward set $D$. This is the unique, hence inclusion-minimal, outward set for that order. Contracting $f$ returns $C$, but every corner order of $C$ begins at its unique corner $0$, so no record with boundary order $(2,0)$ survives. Thus same-order attainability with a smaller outward set is not contraction-monotone, even after keeping only inclusion-minimal outward sets. The lost record cannot by itself destroy positive gluing because compatibility with it forces every other piece to have empty outward set and hence to peel to $D$.
verification: The defining class, forced first corners, and the two orders are preserved in the manuscript; its original replay artifact is papers/dismantlable-ample/research/boundary_attainability_failure.py/json.
